comments.body:
PLAN-REVIEW STATUS (3 cycles, still BLOCK — deep AC5 spec gap). Cycle 1: transient LLMUnavailableError. Cycle 2 (real): 2 G6 blocks — AC5 mechanism unspecified, AC10 equivalence contradicted its own deletion blind-spot. Remediated both (chose merge-onto-prior-snapshot; scoped AC10 to observable classes). Cycle 3 surfaced 4 DEEPER code-grounded blocks that invalidate that mechanism:
1) AC1 invalidates tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py::test_dc_backend_is_deliberately_not_incremental (asserts DC is NOT incremental) — AC7 must enumerate its disposition (delete or invert to assert DC now satisfies SupportsIncremental).
2) AC5 merge base is UNSOUND as written: the persisted prior snapshot (.tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/prev_snapshot.json, written by reconcile.py _write_prev_snapshot_key_set ~L557) is KEY-MEMBERSHIP ONLY with empty bodies ({jira_key: {}}), not full content — so upsert-by-key cannot reconstruct a complete curr_snapshot. fetcher.py:751-754 writes a full snapshot to bridge_state/snapshots/<pass>.json but it is DIAGNOSTIC/ephemeral and never loaded into the diff path.
3) The prior snapshot is available in reconcile.py _load_snapshots (ctx.prev_snapshot, ~L263-299), NOT in fetcher.py _build_snapshot (which takes no prior-snapshot arg). Relocate AC5 there or thread prior state in explicitly.
4) AC5 must mandate a FULL-SCAN FALLBACK (not incremental merge) whenever the merge base is empty/missing/corrupt (fresh run: prev_snapshot=={}; or _handle_corrupt_snapshot path), with a test pinning that an incremental fetch onto an empty base never reaches the differ as a standalone/partial snapshot. AC2 currently gates fallback on isinstance (capability presence), not on merge-base availability.
NEXT: rewrite AC5 to either (a) SCOPE persisting a full-content prior curr_snapshot as the merge base + carry-forward unchanged keys + full-scan fallback on empty/corrupt base, OR (b) confine incremental to a field-update path that NEVER feeds absence/edge detection (which keeps requiring a full scan). Then fix AC7 test disposition, re-run review-plan. reconcile.py snapshot model confirmed by direct read.

compiled_state.description:
Remove the dead `SupportsIncremental` capability and its false docstring, so the reconciler
backend port stops asserting a dispatch behaviour that does not exist.

## Context / Problem

`SupportsIncremental` (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py:545-553`) is a
`@runtime_checkable` capability Protocol whose docstring asserts, in the present tense, a
behaviour that is not implemented:

> Core uses an incremental fetch only when ``isinstance(backend, SupportsIncremental)``;
> otherwise it falls back to a full scan.

It has **zero implementers** and **zero dispatch**: no adapter defines `search_incremental`, and
no `isinstance(backend, SupportsIncremental)` check exists anywhere in `src/` (confirmed by
`grep -rn "SupportsIncremental" src/` — the only hits are the class itself and the module-docstring
inventory at `_backend.py:11-19`). A tested, documented, maintained capability that is never
invoked is a false-assurance signal: a reader auditing the backend port finds a "core uses this"
promise the code never keeps.

This is the same defect class the sibling ticket `723f-c5b2-d83b-43cb` (closed, this epic)
resolved — a docstring that "actively lies" about a zero-caller unit — and it resolved it by
**deleting** the dead unit. No consumer needs an incremental fetch: the three tickets that
`depends_on` this one (`0743`, `373f`, `fc0c`) are unrelated janitor items, and the reconciler's
full-scan fetch (`fetcher.py` `_build_snapshot`) is the only fetch path in use.

## Approach

**Delete the dead declaration** so reality (a backend port with no incremental fetch) no longer
needs a claim that contradicts it. This is the minimal, correctness-neutral remedy for a
false-assurance finding and matches the epic's established handling of the identical defect class
(`723f` deleted `bug_close_reason_ok` and the dead `_attestation` module). Because the capability
has no dispatch and no implementers, removing it changes **no** externally observable reconciler
behaviour — the full scan already runs unconditionally.

Two negative tests reference the Protocol and must be disposed of; both are safe to remove
(removal-rationale, Chesterton's Fence):

- `test_backends_without_incremental_are_detected`
  (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_capability.py:68-69`) guards that the isinstance
  **skip branch** detects a backend lacking a capability. Triggering scenario the fence protects:
  a backend that declines a capability must not be driven through it. That scenario stays covered
  after removal by `FakeBackend` declining `SupportsLinks` — `test_fake_backend_does_not_advertise_links`
  (`:33-34`) and `test_link_sync_is_skipped_for_a_backend_without_the_capability` (`:42-48`) exercise
  the same skip branch — so deleting the incremental-specific case drops **no unique** coverage.
- `test_dc_backend_is_deliberately_not_incremental`
  (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py:85-89`) carries an explicit
  intent marker: its docstring says the assertion exists "to stop it being added by accident."
  With the `SupportsIncremental` Protocol itself removed, there is no capability to accidentally
  opt into, so the fence's purpose is fully subsumed by the deletion; the design rationale it
  recorded (no client need, and incremental fetch has its own correctness surface) is preserved in
  this ticket and in the ADR 0035 amendment below.

ADR 0035 names `SupportsIncremental` in exactly one place — the opt-in-capability prose paragraph
`docs/adr/0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md:191-195`, with the symbol on `:192`
("`SupportsLinks`, `SupportsComments`, `SupportsIncremental`"). That paragraph and the summary at
`:259` also assert a "**three** opt-in capability Protocols" **count**, which becomes two once the
capability is removed. ADRs are durable records, so this is an **amendment**, not a text deletion,
using the repo's established `> **AMENDED by [rebar:<id>]**` convention already present in that
file.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py` — delete the `SupportsIncremental` class
  (`:545-553`) and drop `:class:\`SupportsIncremental\`` from the module-docstring opt-in inventory
  (`:11-19`), leaving `SupportsLinks` and `SupportsComments`.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_capability.py` — remove the `SupportsIncremental`
  import (`:16`) and delete `test_backends_without_incremental_are_detected` (`:68-69`); retain the
  `SupportsLinks` skip-path tests unchanged.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py` — remove the
  `SupportsIncremental` import (`:35`) and delete `test_dc_backend_is_deliberately_not_incremental`
  (`:85-89`); retain `test_dc_backend_advertises_its_three_capabilities` (`:78-82`) unchanged.
- `docs/adr/0035-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md` — amend the opt-in-capability paragraph
  (`:191-195`, symbol at `:192`) and the "three ... capability Protocols" count at `:191` and
  `:259` via the `> **AMENDED by [rebar:1de3-a19f-c4ea-4b28]**` convention.

No adapter or fetcher file is touched: there is nothing to implement.

## Testing

This is a dead-code removal that adds no new runtime behaviour, so the verification is a
regression check plus a coverage-preservation check, both at the in-process unit tier against the
real Protocols and backends:

- **Regression oracle.** After the edits, the reconciler capability suite is green:
  `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_capability.py tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py`
  collects and passes with the two deleted tests gone and no import error for the removed symbol.
- **Coverage-preservation oracle (the fence).** `test_link_sync_is_skipped_for_a_backend_without_the_capability`
  still collects and passes, proving the isinstance skip branch — a backend declining a capability
  is not driven through it — remains covered by the retained `SupportsLinks` negative case.
- **Absence oracle.** `grep -rq "SupportsIncremental" src/ tests/` exits non-zero, proving the
  declaration and every test reference are gone (the only surviving reference is the amended ADR
  prose under `docs/`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The `SupportsIncremental` class is removed from `_backend.py`
      (verified: `grep -rq "class SupportsIncremental" src/` exits non-zero — no match).
- [ ] The `_backend.py` module-docstring opt-in-capability inventory (`:11-19`) no longer names
      `SupportsIncremental` and lists only `SupportsLinks` and `SupportsComments`
      (verified by reading the docstring).
- [ ] `test_backends_without_incremental_are_detected` and the `SupportsIncremental` import are
      removed from `test_backend_capability.py`, and the retained skip-path tests
      `test_fake_backend_does_not_advertise_links` and
      `test_link_sync_is_skipped_for_a_backend_without_the_capability` still pass
      (verified: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_capability.py` is green).
- [ ] `test_dc_backend_is_deliberately_not_incremental` and the `SupportsIncremental` import are
      removed from `test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py`, and
      `test_dc_backend_advertises_its_three_capabilities` still passes
      (verified: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py` is green).
- [ ] ADR 0035's opt-in-capability paragraph (`:191-195`, symbol at `:192`) and its "three ...
      capability Protocols" count at `:191` and `:259` are amended via the
      `> **AMENDED by [rebar:1de3-a19f-c4ea-4b28]**` convention to record that `SupportsIncremental`
      was removed as a zero-implementer, unwired capability (count now two), with a one-line note
      that an updated-since fetch can be reintroduced from vendor support (Jira JQL `updated >`,
      GitHub `since=`, Linear `updatedAt`) if a measured bandwidth need later arises
      (verified by reading the amended ADR).
- [ ] No reference to `SupportsIncremental` remains in `src/` or `tests/`
      (verified: `grep -rq "SupportsIncremental" src/ tests/` exits non-zero — no match; the only
      surviving reference is the amended ADR under `docs/`).

remove the SupportsIncremental import and the test_backends_without_incremental_are_detected negative test; retain the SupportsLinks skip-path tests
remove the SupportsIncremental import and the test_dc_backend_is_deliberately_not_incremental test
amend the capability-inventory to record SupportsIncremental removal via the AMENDED-by convention
